answer.rationale: . The write path latency spike of 5x target at p99 is a hard limit on checkout writes. Circuit breakers on the payments dependency (memory_b4) proved exactly this pattern: when a dependency degrades, failing fast protects the rest of the checkout path and latency recovers the same day. Today's conditions—heavy write traffic at peak settlement—match that context. Enabling a circuit breaker now prevents cascading failures while the system is already under load, preserving sustained availability without losing writes. The other options are lower fit: rollback_release risks losing in-flight writes during a peak; regional_failover takes too long to stabilize; add_capacity would need provisioning time beyond the 90‑minute window; route_read_replicas only helps read traffic, not the write path bottleneck.
